_why: Measured state of the mission's offline promise, kept in the repo so a passing build is not mistaken for a kept promise.
method: Chrome DevTools Protocol (playwright is not installed on the build host): load the built game from a local static server, warm the cache, set Network.emulateNetworkConditions offline=true, reload, and read window.__GAME__ and the active scene list. Probe committed at scripts/lib/offline-probe.py.

result.observed: window.__GAME__ present, game.isRunning true, TitleScene active, and the real menu rendered - not the browser's error page.

before.observed: Chrome's ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED page. window.__GAME__ absent, zero active scenes.
before.cause: Nothing cached the game. Every request was already same-origin, which is necessary for offline play but not sufficient: with no service worker the browser still had to reach the server, so a cold reload could not even fetch index.html.

how_it_works: scripts/gen-service-worker.mjs runs after the game builds and writes a per-game sw.js plus a guarded registration snippet into index.html. It precaches the cold-load set (index.html and everything index.html references: JS chunks and fonts) on install, then caches same-origin responses as they are first used, which is how Phaser's sprites and audio survive going offline. Navigation requests fall back to the cached index.html so a reload with no network boots the game instead of the browser's error page. The cache name carries a hash of the precache list so a new build replaces the old cache rather than serving a stale bundle.
not_yet_measured: kingshot, lastwar and champs have generated workers from the same script but were not probed; only whiteout and wirework were.

Deep offline play - reaching a scene whose sprites were never fetched while online. Those are runtime-cached on first use, so an asset never touched while online is still unavailable offline by design.
The probe is a maintainer tool, not part of `npm run build`: it needs a live browser, so the build gates the precondition (check:selfhosted) rather than the boot.
